text:
maya (AE): Heads-up — ACME POC running into slow first-byte / first-token for interactive flows. Demo in ~2h, customer blocked. Can @sam @alex jump in?

sam (SRE): On it. Are they on Dedicated or hosted? Any request IDs or an example call we can repro with?

maya (AE): Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (dedicated-us-west-2-poc-123). Customer sent this sample call + headers:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-acme" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-70b","input":"Summarize the last quarter results in 3 bullets","max_tokens":120}'
```

maya (AE): They say TTFT ~900ms-1.2s on first request, subsequent tokens stream okay.

jesse (Solutions Eng): Pasted a short log snippet from the Dedicated node (redacted ids):

```text
[2026-02-12T14:10:03Z] req=req_01F4 queue_len=11 batch_id=42 kv_cache=miss token_gen_delay=340ms
[2026-02-12T14:10:03Z] req=req_01F4 rate_limit=429 route=/v1/generate retries=1
[2026-02-12T14:10:04Z] req=req_01F5 queue_len=2 batch_id=43 kv_cache=hit token_gen_delay=28ms
[2026-02-12T14:10:05Z] node=dedicated-1 status=busy max_batch=8 cur_batch=12
```

alex (ML Eng): Two likely issues from that snippet: 1) kv_cache entries are missing for interactive prefixes -> first-request pays full decoding cost. 2) queue_len/cur_batch mismatch: client concurrency is creating microbursts that exceed max_batch, so requests pile up waiting for batch assembly -> high TTFT. Also 429s indicate route-level throttling (customer is using high concurrency with low quota per route).

sam (SRE): Quick checks: ask customer to confirm they are not setting `X-Disable-KV: true` or using ephemeral zero-cache headers. Also ask what client concurrency and per-connection keepalive they have.

maya (AE): Customer confirms no explicit disable header. They are using our JS SDK with default concurrency override: concurrency=16, and their client is single-instance orchestrator making parallel calls.

alex (ML Eng): Fix suggestions:
- Enable prefix KV cache on the route/deployment (kv_cache=true)
- Increase `max_batch_size` on the Dedicated pool to 12 or 16 to absorb bursts
- Alternatively reduce client concurrency to 6-8 for interactive flows so batches form faster and don't back up
- Set route policy `prefer_low_latency=true` for interactive endpoints to bias the runtime toward smaller batches and faster scheduling

jesse (Solutions Eng): Sending a small command they can run against the admin API to toggle cache & batching quickly:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://controlplane.redwood.run/pools/dedicated-us-west-2-poc-123/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"kv_cache":true,"continuous_batching":true,"max_batch_size":12}'
```

jesse (Solutions Eng): Also attaching a short explainer for pricing impact: batching increases throughput and reduces cost per token for steady workloads. For interactive demos we typically trade a small TTFT increase (median first-token from ~220ms -> ~260-320ms depending on batch/window) for 2-4x lower cost-per-token under heavy concurrency. If they prefer strict sub-250ms TTFT, use `prefer_low_latency=true` and smaller `max_batch_size` but expect higher unit costs.

maya (AE): Customer asked if enabling kv_cache has any security/PII implications.

sam (SRE): KV cache only stores model key-value prefixes (not user payload). For Dedicated it's stored on the node and encrypted at rest if KMS is enabled. I'll confirm audit log entries and SLA implications.

alex (ML Eng): Operational note — for the particular model they picked (redwood-llama-70b), warmup of a KV cache on first request can be expensive. If they have predictable prefixes, pre-populating cache with a small warmup script helps the first request in demos. Example warmup script: 

```bash
# run a warmup set to populate KV
for p in "Summarize the last quarter" "List top 3 risk items"; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-acme" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"model\":\"redwood-llama-70b\",\"input\":\"$p\",\"max_tokens\":8}"
done
```

jesse (Solutions Eng): Action items:
- sam: toggle kv_cache + bump max_batch_size to 12 on the pool and watch for immediate TTFT change (I can assist).
- alex: provide a 1-pager with numbers for tradeoffs and a recommended warmup set.
- maya: explain pricing delta to customer and check security Q answers.
- jesse: schedule follow-up demo at 14:30 PT.

infra-bot: deploy started for pool `dedicated-us-west-2-poc-123` with config change (kv_cache=true, max_batch_size=12). ETA ~2m. :rocket:

maya (AE): Thanks team — will share notes with ACME and confirm whether they want demo at 14:30 or later. :thumbsup:
